text:
maria: heads up — we saw a sudden p99 latency jump on the small-seq traffic after last night's infra deploy. started ~03:10 UTC, affecting two ash clusters. p99 doubled from ~220ms to ~480ms.

alex: which deploy? driver change or runtime patch?

maria: infra deploy shows driver roll (540.70) + autoscaler tweak. deploy-bot posted: "driver: nvidia-driver-540.70 applied to pool-ash-2 at 03:00 UTC". infra-bot also flagged higher kernel autoselect counts.

sam: can you paste perf profile + kernel selection logs? need both kernel names and sequence length histogram.

maria: pasted a trimmed snippet from the runtime profiler: 
```
[2026-02-11T03:09:58Z] model=redwood-7b variant=fp16 seq=16 batch=1 kernel=flash_attn_v2 launches=742 p99=460ms
[2026-02-11T03:09:58Z] model=redwood-7b variant=fp16 seq=64 batch=2 kernel=triton_attention launches=120 p99=210ms
[2026-02-11T03:09:58Z] kv_cache_hits=0.2 kv_evictions=0.18 gpu_mem_free_mb=1024
```
maria: note lots of small seqs being routed to flash_attn_v2 unexpectedly. before deploy those were mostly using triton_attention.

alex: interesting. driver update likely changed heuristics (or driver performance characteristics) causing our kernel selector to prefer flash for seq<=32. we have a path that prefers lower FLOPS kernel based on occupancy estimates. if driver changes timing of kernels, selector weights flip.

jen: any evidence of noisy neighbor or contention? could be co-located VMs causing higher L2 miss / TLB pressure making flash slower.

maria: host metrics show one VM on same host had 80% SM utilization around the window. noisy-neighbor patterns match. but we also see kernel benchmark micro-bench results shifted post-driver: flash_attn microbench is ~15% slower on 540.70 than 535.x on short sequences.

rachel: I ran quick microbench on an identical GPU image locally: 
```
# run: ./bench_attention --seq 16 --dtype fp16
535.86: flash_attn_v2 = 3.2 ms  triton_attention = 3.6 ms
540.70: flash_attn_v2 = 3.9 ms  triton_attention = 3.4 ms
```
rachel: so ranking flipped at seq=16. selector uses relative latencies; it picked flash previously but now it's slower.

alex: that would explain p99 increase. flash kernel has higher per-launch overhead and is sensitive to L2 behavior -> noisy neighbor magnifies it. combined effect -> p99 spike.

sam: immediate mitigation options: 1) force kernel policy to prefer triton for seq<=32 on affected pools, 2) pin noisy VMs away, 3) roll back driver. best short-term is policy tweak + canary.

maria: I pushed a canary config to pool-ash-2 to bias selector to triton for seq<=32. will monitor.

deploy-bot: config-change: runtime/kernel-policy updated on pool-ash-2 by maria at 03:28 UTC (bias: prefer triton for seq<=32).

ops-bot: alert resolved? p99 trending down to ~230ms after policy change at 03:40 UTC.

jen: great. for root cause: we should log kernel microbench results at deploy time and record selector thresholds. also add a quick validation job on driver upgrades that runs short seq microbench to detect rank flips.

alex: +1. action list: 
- sam: create driver-upgrade validation job (bench flash vs triton seq=8/16/32) — due EOD
- rachel: add metric to selector service for kernel microbench history per driver version — due 48h
- maria: run a backfill analysis across clusters to see how many pools saw flips — due 24h
- infra: consider conservative policy for driver rollouts to low-risk pools first — infra team

maria: noted. I'll keep this thread updated with the cluster-level CSV I'm generating. thanks for quick responses :thumbsup:

alex: please follow up with a short postmortem once root cause confirmed. include workload distribution, microbench numbers, and proposed selector hardening.

maria: will do.
